content: 1. Porter RM, Goldin S, Lafond KE, Hedman L, Ungkuldee M, Kurzum J, et al. (2020) conducted an analysis to determine whether seasonal influenza programs enhance pandemic preparedness. Their study focused on vaccine deployment during the 2009 influenza pandemic, published in Vaccine (38(5):1152–1159). 2. Rockman S, Taylor B, McCauley JW, Barr IG, Longstaff R, Bahra R (2022) explored global pandemic preparedness by optimizing capabilities based on influenza experiences. Their findings were published in Vaccines (10(4):589). 3. Savage R, Whelan M, Johnson I, Rea E, LaFreniere M, Rosella LC, et al. (2011) assessed secondary attack rates among household contacts during the early stages of the H1N1 influenza pandemic in Ontario, Canada (April–June 2009). This prospective observational study was published in BMC Public Health (11:234). 4. Saxenian H (2017) developed a resource guide on immunization financing for advocates, policymakers, and program managers, accessible through the United Nations University International Institute for Global Health. 5. The United Nations University International Institute for Global Health (2021) provided a guidance note and checklist for addressing gender-related barriers to equitable COVID-19 vaccine deployment. 6. Van Kerkhove MD, Hirve S, Koukounari A, Mounts AW, and the H1N1pdm serology working group (2013) conducted a meta-analysis estimating age-specific cumulative incidence during the 2009 influenza pandemic. Their work was published in Influenza and Other Respiratory Viruses (7(5):872–886). 7. The World Health Organization (WHO) (2023a) released the Preparedness and Resilience for Emerging Threats (PRET) Module 1, focusing on planning for respiratory pathogen pandemics. 8. WHO (2023b) published guidance on developing and implementing national deployment and vaccination plans for pandemic influenza and other respiratory viruses with pandemic potential. 9. WHO (2023c) provided insights into COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness through its Immunization Analysis and Insights platform. 10. WHO (2022a) conducted a global analysis of COVID-19 intra-action reviews to reflect on and improve country emergency preparedness and response during pandemics. 11. WHO (2022b) outlined the Emergency Use Listing Procedure (Version 9, August 2022) for medical products. 12. WHO (2022c) proposed ten strategies to strengthen global health emergency preparedness, response, and resilience. 13. WHO (2022d) released a roadmap for prioritizing the use of COVID-19 vaccines, emphasizing equitable distribution. 14. WHO (2022e) provided interim guidance on public health surveillance for COVID-19. 15. WHO (2021a) issued guidance on developing national deployment and vaccination plans for COVID-19 vaccines. 16. WHO (2021b) updated the Pandemic Influenza Preparedness (PIP) Framework to enhance virus sharing and access to vaccines. 17. WHO (2021c) reported on the H1N1 vaccine deployment initiative, highlighting lessons learned. 18. WHO (2021d) revised the Global Benchmarking Tool (GBT) for evaluating national regulatory systems for medical products. 19. WHO (2021e) published the 55th report of the Expert Committee on Specifications for Pharmaceutical Preparations. 20. WHO (2021f) provided interim recommendations for heterologous COVID-19 vaccine schedules. 21. WHO (2021g) held a technical consultation on managing the COVID-19 infodemic, calling for action to address misinformation. 22. WHO (2021h) developed a competency framework to build a workforce capable of managing infodemics. 23. WHO (2021i) issued an aide-memoire on infection prevention and control principles for COVID-19 vaccination activities. 24. WHO (2021j) released a guide for post-introduction evaluation of COVID-19 vaccines. 25. WHO (2021k) introduced a COVID-19 Exercise Programme to support vaccine deployment drills. 26. WHO (2020a) developed a values framework for allocating and prioritizing COVID-19 vaccination. 27. WHO (2020b) launched a training program for health workers on COVID-19 vaccination through the OpenWHO platform. 28. WHO (2020c) published a safety surveillance manual for COVID-19 vaccines. 29. WHO (2019a) provided guidelines on import procedures for medical products. 30. WHO (2019b) reviewed technologies for treating infectious and sharp waste from healthcare facilities. 31. WHO (2019c) released a user manual for causality assessment of adverse events following immunization (AEFI). 32. WHO (2017a) issued guidelines on regulatory preparedness for pandemic influenza vaccines in non-vaccine-producing countries. 33. WHO (2017b) updated its guidance for surveillance during an influenza pandemic. 34. WHO (2017c) published a guide on evaluating influenza vaccine effectiveness through observational studies. 35. WHO (2016a) provided guidance on managing ethical issues during infectious disease outbreaks. 36. WHO (2016b) updated its global manual on surveillance of adverse events following immunization. 37. WHO (2015) released a practical guide for health staff on immunization practices. 38. WHO (2013) issued guidelines for independent lot release of vaccines by regulatory authorities. 39. WHO (2012) provided guidance on developing national deployment and vaccination plans for pandemic influenza vaccines. 40. WHO (2010) introduced a post-introduction evaluation tool for new vaccines. 41. WHO (2009) reported on the extraordinary meeting of the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts (SAGE) on Immunization during the H1N1 pandemic. 42. WHO (2006a) published the World Health Report 2006, emphasizing global health workforce collaboration. 43. WHO (2006b) provided guidelines for managing waste from injection activities at the district level. 44. WHO and UNICEF (2021) outlined considerations for monitoring COVID-19 vaccination data collection and use. 45. WHO, UNICEF, and Gavi (2021) emphasized the importance of gender considerations in the Immunization Agenda 2030. This content reflects a comprehensive body of work addressing pandemic preparedness, vaccine deployment, and public health strategies, with a focus on lessons learned from past pandemics and the COVID-19 response.
